title: Kids Across America Share What Freedom Means to Them on the Country's 250th Birthday
summary: What does America mean to you? That's the big question NPR asked kids all over the country for the nation's 250th birthday. More than 700 students sent in podcasts—short audio stories—about the American experience. Some talked to their immigrant grandparents. One girl, Livie, interviewed her grandpa about leaving Greece. "Very hard. Very very hard," he told her. But he worked in a factory, dreamed big, and opened his own restaurants. Other kids dug into history. Fourth graders Travis and Oliver researched the Underground Railroad, a secret network that helped around 100,000 slaves escape to freedom. They even interviewed an expert! High schooler Grace lives in Takoma Park, Maryland, one of the few places where 16-year-olds can vote in local elections. She and her friend Angelika made a podcast about the power of the youth vote. They say voting makes young people learn about government and get involved. Some stories were serious. Ursula shared how her grandpa still suffers from the Vietnam War, even though he came home alive. Violet talked to her mom, a veteran who served in Iraq, about not taking freedom for granted. The winning podcasts show that America means many things: hard work, courage, family, and speaking up. Which story would you tell?
why_it_matters: This story shows that even kids your age can share powerful stories about what freedom and family mean, and your voice can be heard.

background_read: The United States turned 250 years old in 2026, celebrating the anniversary of the Declaration of Independence.
NPR (a radio and online service that shares news and stories) asked kids to share what America means to them.
Some kids talked about the Underground Railroad, a secret network that helped around 100,000 slaves escape before the Civil War.
Article_Structure: WHO: Students from across the United States, including Livie, Travis, Oliver, Grace, Ursula, and Violet.
WHAT: They created short podcasts (audio stories) answering the question 'What does America mean to you?'
WHERE: The podcasts came from everywhere in the country, with one story from Takoma Park, Maryland.
WHY: To celebrate the nation's 250th birthday and share personal stories about freedom, courage, and family.

perspectives.description: Livie's grandpa shows that with hard work and big dreams, people can build a new life in America, even after a tough start.
By learning about the Underground Railroad, kids remember that freedom was won through bravery and that many people risked everything to be free.
Grace and Angelika believe voting at 16 helps young people learn about government and get involved, showing that teenagers can make a difference.
